questions_and_answers.question: Which is the correct way to say ‘I helped him’ using a noun-plus-करना construction?

articles.text: Hindi verbs can combine with the auxiliaries 'है' and 'था' using the same past participial forms. When a dire  ct object is marked by 'को', it is in the oblique case and does not influence the verb; the verb remains in a neutral masculine singular form. For example: 'मैंने उनको देखा' (I saw them) or 'उन्होंने साड़ियों को बेचा' (they sold the saris). Because the object is marked by 'को', the verb ends in the neutral masculine form. If the direct object appears without 'को' in the direct case, it controls the verb’s gender and number. Thus 'मैंने साड़ियाँ देखीं' shows a feminine plural agreement on 'देखीं', and sentences like 'किसी ने चिट्ठी भेजी' or 'हमने बहुत सवाल पूछे' show the verb agreeing with an unmarked feminine or masculine plural object. A small group of verbs—करना (to do), देना (to give), लेना (to take), and पीना (to drink)—have contracted past forms: masculine singular (किया, दिया, लिया, पिया), masculine plural (किये, दिये, लिये, पिये), feminine singular (की, दी, ली, पी), and feminine plural (कीं, दीं, लीं, पीं). The masculine plural forms may also be written with ए endings such as किये, दिये, etc. In noun-plus-करना constructions, the verb करना agrees with the noun, as in 'मैंने आपका इंतज़ार किया' (I waited for you), 'मैंने उनकी मदद की' (I helped him/her), and 'मैंने आपसे मिलने की कोशिश की' (I tried to see you).
